faq.q: Can I resize using centimetres or inches, not just pixels?
faq.a: Yes. Pick a unit (px, cm, mm or inch) and set a DPI (default 300); the tool converts physical sizes to pixels using that DPI — so 3.5×4.5 cm at 300 DPI becomes the right pixel count. DPI only matters for physical/print units; for pixels it's ignored. Remember DPI is a print instruction, not detail stored in the file.

Government/ID presets: Passport (3.5×4.5 cm), US Visa (2×2 inch), SSC Form (150×200 px), UPSC (110×140 px), Bank PO (200×230 px), Signature (3.5×1.5 cm and 140×60 px) and Square 400×400. Social presets: Instagram Post (1080×1080) and Story (1080×1920), Facebook Cover, LinkedIn Banner, Twitter Header, Passport (413×531) and YouTube Thumbnail (1280×720).

faq.q: Will resizing stretch my photo, and can I enlarge?
faq.a: Keep 'Keep aspect ratio' ticked and width/height stay linked so the image isn't distorted (presets turn the lock off to force exact dimensions). You can enlarge with 1.5x/2x/3x/4x buttons or a scale-by percentage, with high-quality smoothing and an optional 'Sharpen after resize'. Note enlarging interpolates pixels — start from the largest original you have.

faq.q: Can I resize a whole folder at once?
faq.a: Yes. Drop multiple images and a 'Resize all as ZIP' button appears; it applies the same settings to each, keeping each image's own aspect ratio when the lock is on (so differently shaped photos aren't distorted). You can also copy a single resized image to the clipboard. Output can be PNG, JPG or WebP, and your settings are remembered between visits.
